slice: Slice 5 — declarative entity lifecycle (unified kind-level lifecycle clause: declaration + fold-view hide + folded-state validate warn)
thesis: Add ONE kind-level KDL clause (working name `lifecycle`) that declares a kind's lifecycle field and its active/terminal state set, subsuming the three previously-parallel proposals: the domain-neutral lifecycle-field marker (grammar-domain-neutrality), the fold-view hide of terminal-status rows (status-aware-kind-budget, now the first tenant not a sibling), and the enum home in the kind-defined declaration document (payload-constraints-in-declarations). The clause flows through the existing declared-semantics pipeline (AST -> declaration document -> FoldSection -> Surface KindView -> budget()), hides inactive entities from the DEFAULT fold view only, with honest Window.limited_by provenance, `--all` defeat, and auto-disable when an explicit lifecycle-field predicate is present. Inactive nodes keep their salience contribution and stay reachable via --refs (the hide is a budget-stage projection over primary rows, applied strictly AFTER project() has materialized salience/tiers/inbound-edges over the full population). A folded-state active-targets-inactive warn is added to the `loops validate` surface. SPEC-9 pricing (below) shows this lands loops-side behind a documented spec-delta note without blocking the loops-go oracle.
current_behavior: Kind-block clauses parsed today are fold/boundary/search/parse/preview/edge only — libs/lang/src/lang/loader.py:384-443 (`_load_loop_def`); there is no lifecycle/hide clause. `LoopDef` (libs/lang/src/lang/ast.py:501-511) carries folds/boundary/search/parse/preview_fields/edges, no lifecycle. The kind-defined declaration document round-trip (`_loop_def_to_payload`/`_loop_def_from_payload`, libs/lang/src/lang/document.py:461-485) serializes exactly those six facets — this is the SPEC §9.2 `_decl.kind-defined` payload schema. `budget()` (apps/loops/src/loops/surface.py:873-914) implements limit/last/salience_window slices and records Window.limited_by in {"limit","last","salience",None} (Window docstring surface.py:115); it has NO status/lifecycle hide, and `salience_window` is a latent param wired to no flag (grep: surface.py:878 only). Salience/inbound/tier are materialized ONCE in project() over ALL rows (surface.py:602 salience, 642 `_assign_tiers`, 657 inbound_edges) before any budget transform runs — so a post-project row-drop naturally preserves the edge-position invariant. FoldSection (libs/atoms/src/atoms/fold_state.py:112-123) carries preview_fields + edge_fields but no lifecycle; vertex_reader builds it from loop_def at libs/engine/src/engine/vertex_reader.py:934-961. `--all` does NOT exist in the read grammar (grep: present only for ls/population, ls_args.py:59, population.py:43 — NOT read_args.py). `loops validate` (apps/loops/src/loops/commands/devtools.py:20-107 + lenses/validate.py) validates FILE SYNTAX ONLY via lang.validate(ast) — it never opens a store or inspects folded state / edge targets, so no folded-state validate surface exists yet. loops-go has ZERO §9 declaration-layer code (grep for kind-defined/_decl/lifecycle/declaration across loops-go/atoms,store,internal returns nothing); SPEC.md marks §9 PROVISIONAL/design-led and only §1-6 atoms are oracle-certified.

Add an `elif child.name == "lifecycle":` branch in _load_loop_def (near the `edge` branch at loader.py:418-441): parse `lifecycle "<field>" active="..."` (or terminal=), reject duplicates/malformed. Add the AST import.

Add a lang-type-free lifecycle field to FoldSection (fold_state.py:112-123), mirroring edge_fields — e.g. `lifecycle: tuple[str, tuple[str, ...]] | None = None` (field name + active/terminal values).
Extract loop_def.lifecycle into the new FoldSection field where edge_specs/preview_fields are extracted (vertex_reader.py:934-961).

Add `show_all: bool = False` to SurfaceSpec (operation.py:38-63) fed from --all.
Add a `--all` store_true flag to the read parser (does not exist today).

In _project_surface budget step (dispatch.py:177-178), gate the lifecycle hide: apply UNLESS spec.show_all, OR (per-kind) the kind's lifecycle field appears in spec.where (auto-disable on explicit predicate). Read the lifecycle field name from the projected surface.schema.
Surface the hidden count in the fold footer, mirroring the window.unindexed footer (fold.py:610-616) and the `(N more)` collapse (884-886): e.g. `(N inactive hidden — --all)`.

VALIDATION HOME. Extend _run_validate (devtools.py:20-107) with a folded-state pass: when a store is resolvable, fold it, and for each active entity carrying an edge/ref to a target whose lifecycle field is terminal/inactive, collect a warn. This is net-new folded-state surface (see open question on scope).
Render the active-targets-inactive warns (validate.py:17-64) as a non-fatal WARN tier distinct from the syntax pass/fail rows.

Per-package gates: uv run --package lang / atoms / engine / loops pytest; ./dev check at repo root.
acceptance_criteria: A single kind-level `lifecycle` clause is parseable, round-trips through the _decl.kind-defined declaration document losslessly, and reaches the read path as FoldSection/KindView metadata — status-aware-kind-budget's `hide` ships as the first tenant of this clause, NOT as a separate sibling clause.
Default `sl read <vertex>` omits terminal/inactive entities of a lifecycle-declaring kind from the FOLD VIEW only; `--facts` (event history) is unchanged; both text and --json see the identical cut.
Window records limited_by="status" with honest shown/total (+ hidden count); the human read shows a footer naming the hidden count and the --all defeat.
`--all` shows everything; an explicit predicate on the lifecycle field auto-disables the hide for that read (per declaring kind).

Inactive entities' inbound edges KEEP counting toward salience (visible rows' salience/tier unchanged by the hide) and inactive nodes STAY reachable in --refs — the hide is never an edge rewrite; retract remains the distinct correction tombstone.
The `loops validate` surface emits a non-fatal active-targets-inactive warn over folded state (not lang declaration validation).

Acceptance is demonstrated by a REAL deprecation walked end-to-end in a test vertex (declare -> emit -> transition to terminal -> observe all of the above), since the live corpus holds zero inactive entities.

SPEC-9 pricing delivered: the lifecycle facet lands loops-side behind a documented SPEC §9.2 spec-delta note, adds NO frozen _decl.* kind, does NOT bump DECLARATION_PROTOCOL_VERSION, and does not block on the loops-go oracle (which has no §9 code today).
measures: SPEC-9 pricing verdict (the required deliverable): (a) frozen _decl.* KIND vocabulary UNCHANGED — lifecycle is a payload FIELD on the existing _decl.kind-defined document (SPEC §9.2 'full loop definition' row), categorically unlike decl-lens-tombstone-vocab-gap which needs a NEW frozen kind; (b) loops-go must mirror `lifecycle` in its kind-defined document schema WHEN it implements §9 — today it has zero §9 code, so nothing to mirror against; (c) verdict = LANDS loops-side behind a SPEC.md §9.2 spec-delta note, does NOT block the oracle, does NOT bump protocol version (bumping would make old readers fail-closed on the whole genesis; the §9.2 forward-compat rule 'unknown fields inside a document are ignored' is the sanctioned path for additive fields).
Number of inactive entities hidden in the acceptance test (must be >0 — a real deprecation, contract-prospective since the live corpus is 0).
Salience-retention delta: visible rows' salience and tier must be byte-identical with vs without the hide applied (target: 0 delta) — the operational proof of the edge-position invariant.
Test count added and the full ./dev check gate green.
risks: Scope creep via the validate surface: `loops validate` has no folded-state mode today (devtools.py:20-107 is syntax-only). Building the full --store/--refs/--foreign-refs surface from payload-constraints-in-declarations here could balloon the slice; a minimal targeted edge-scan is safer (see open questions).

Placement error: pushing the hide into project() or the salience/edge corpus (surface.py:152-300, 602, 642, 657) instead of budget() would silently drop inactive nodes' salience contribution and their --refs presence, violating the binding edge-position. The filter MUST stay a post-project budget-stage row-drop scoped to primary (depth==0) rows.

--refs interaction: the hide must skip walked (depth>0) rows or an inactive node explicitly walked-to would vanish, contradicting 'stay in --refs'. Requires an explicit depth guard in the budget filter.

Missing/unknown lifecycle value handling depends on the polarity choice (active-whitelist hides missing values; terminal-blacklist shows them) — a wrong default could hide legitimately-active entities. Tied to the open polarity question.
Golden churn: the new footer disclosure will move many fold goldens; regenerate deliberately (--update-goldens) and eyeball the diff.

Aggregate/combine vertices: confirm the hide behaves on aggregation reads (per-member KindView must carry lifecycle through the union projection) — otherwise the hide silently no-ops on the config-level project aggregation.
dependencies: The shipped internal declaration table / _decl.* document layer (v0.7.0) — libs/lang/src/lang/document.py + libs/engine/src/engine/declaration.py — is the SPEC-9 home the lifecycle facet extends; no new table work needed.
The Surface transform pipeline (project -> filter -> select -> count -> budget) in apps/loops/src/loops/cli/dispatch.py:_project_surface and surface.py — the seam both text and --json go through.
No dependency on graph build-2, digest, or VertexHandle S5 — this slice is self-contained within the declaration + read path.
loops-go coordination is documentation-only (SPEC.md §9.2 spec-delta); no Go code change is required or possible to block on (§9 unimplemented).
open_questions: Clause polarity/vocabulary (genuine design fork): declare the ACTIVE set (whitelist, grammar-domain-neutrality's `lifecycle "status" open="open,in-progress"` framing — hide everything not-active, missing status => hidden) vs the TERMINAL set (blacklist, status-aware-kind-budget's literal `hide status="resolved"` — hide only named terminals, missing status => shown). The two differ on the missing/unknown-status default and on domain-neutrality. Recommendation: whitelist `active=` for domain-neutrality, but the missing-status default is the arbiter's call.

Validate-surface scope (scope fork): build the full folded-state validate surface (`loops validate --store --refs --foreign-refs`) from payload-constraints-in-declarations now, or bolt a minimal targeted active-targets-inactive edge-scan onto `loops validate` and defer the general surface? The acceptance only needs the warn; recommendation is the minimal scan, but this sets precedent for the larger constraint-validation surface.

DECLARATION_PROTOCOL_VERSION (cross-impl consequence, strong recommendation attached): confirm NO bump (1 stays 1) so old/foreign readers ignore the additive lifecycle field rather than fail-closed on the whole genesis. Flagged because it is a store-canonical, cross-implementation decision even though the §9.2 forward-compat rule makes no-bump the clearly-correct path.
